A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ophiuchus framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite retitling, reformatting, and material being moved or removed.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA, segmentation, EHRXQA, report-generation, and ablation results, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original VQA, segmentation, report-generation, and ablation results and adds crop-based comparisons and necessary-tool-calling results.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent, SAM2/BiomedParse/zoom tools, three training stages, self-reflection sampling, and ATRL rewards remain unchanged. The added clarification that tool calls and answers can co-occur does not establish a procedural change; the system and user prompts are retained.

E1.justification: v1's Appendix C.7 and Table 12 evaluate EHRXQA image-related, table-related, and combined image/table questions. This entire evaluation disappears in v2, removing coverage of structured clinical database reasoning. The medical imaging benchmarks and MIMIC-CXR report-generation tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 removes MedVLM-R1 from the main VQA, same-tool, and report-generation comparisons, and removes AURA, SMR-Agents, and MedAgent-Pro from Table 1. The EHRXQA comparison with GPT-5, EHRAgent, AgentMD, and RiskAgent also disappears. A self-cropping Qwen baseline is added, substantially revising the comparison set.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation procedures using self-predicted versus ground-truth crops and measures necessary tool use on cases the base model answers incorrectly. The EHRXQA NeuralSQL, official-split, and execution-accuracy protocol disappears with that evaluation. Settings for retained experiments, including data splits, training budgets, and principal metrics, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 extends the existing investigation of static crops with self-cropping and broader GT-crop comparisons. Table 5 adds necessary-tool-calling analysis alongside previously reported unnecessary-call rates. Training-stage, reward, tool-substitution, hyperparameter, and case analyses remain; the segmentation-tool substitution study is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and training curves remain unchanged; the retained counts of rollout candidates are not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: The reported result set changes substantially through removal of the EHRXQA results and several comparator rows. v2 adds crop-comparison averages of 50.2 for self-cropping and 54.9 for GT crops, plus a reported 93.7% average necessary-tool-calling rate. Matched retained scores remain unchanged, including Ophiuchus's 68.0 out-of-domain VQA average; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v1 Equation 4 explicitly defines the policy probability ratio and group-normalized advantage used in GRPO; v2 omits these definitions while retaining the loss. The cold-start objective moves to Appendix B without substantive change, and the self-reflection and reward equations remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain tool-integrated multimodal reasoning, three-stage training, adaptive tool orchestration, and strong medical benchmark performance. The revised title, abstract, and contribution wording emphasize capabilities already claimed in v1 rather than introducing a new core scientific claim.

C2.justification: New Section 4.4 argues that tool quality, coverage, and complementarity matter more than tool count. Correspondingly, v2 removes v1's limitation concerning having only three tools. It also expands interpretations of selective tool use and crop controls, while retaining the computational-cost, 2D-processing, and failure-case limitations.

D1.justification: v1 promises future release of datasets, code, and models; v2 instead states that project code is available. v2 also adds ethics-approval, consent-waiver, and deidentification information and clarifies co-occurring tool calls and answers. Hardware, hyperparameters, data-construction instructions, and prompt templates are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes references and discussion associated with MedVLM-R1, SMR-Agents, EHRXQA, EHRAgent, AgentMD, and RiskAgent, including the comparison with clinical risk-prediction agents. The principal positioning against fixed-workflow medical agents and segmentation-oriented MLLMs remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and author information and condenses the abstract, conclusion, and selected explanatory passages. It relocates the cold-start objective and tool-substitution discussion, adds discussion and impact statements, and removes the appendix contents and writing-assistance statement. The main narrative sequence and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format with new typography and running headers. Tables move between the main text and appendices, crop and tool-behavior displays are added, and the EHR table is removed. Existing figures and prompts are enlarged or separated onto individual pages, without changing their underlying visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The added crop controls strengthen investigation of the mechanism, but removed EHR and baseline comparisons narrow validation. The new tool-use analysis also has an unresolved inconsistency: under Section 4.3's stated denominator, recovering 90.8% of MedXpertQA base-model failures, given 23.5% base accuracy, implies at least 69.5% overall accuracy, whereas Table 1 reports 39.3%. The PDFs do not resolve whether the rate or its description is wrong, so the benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
